transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for fitting me in. I really appreciate your time. Um, I guess I'm here because... well, I hope this doesn't sound too strange, and I'm sure it might just be stress from work, but... is it okay if I just explain it how it's been feeling? 

I work as a financial advisor here in Cincinnati, and for a while now, I've just been... well, I've been kind of convinced that certain people in the local arts and finance circles are quietly tracking which clients I meet with. And it feels like they're sending me these little signals about it. Just through things like how event invitations are worded, or specific panel topics, or even who gets seated near me at networking dinners. 

I keep telling myself it could just be a coincidence—because I know exactly how it sounds, I really do—but I just can't seem to let it go. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
How long have you been noticing and feeling convinced about these signals and being tracked—weeks, months, or longer?

Um, well, it definitely hasn't been going on forever, I promise. I'd say... maybe it's been about two months? Give or take a little. I think that's when I first started noticing the, um, the patterns with my client meetings and feeling like they were sending those signals. 

But really, it hasn't been that long in the grand scheme of things, and I keep telling myself it's probably just a temporary stress thing, you know? Is two months a normal amount of time to wait before talking to someone about this? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right and not overreacting or wasting your time with something minor.

Over these past two months, have you also noticed any significant changes in your mood—like feeling unusually sad, hopeless, or low, or on the other end, unusually energetic, elated, or needing much less sleep than normal?

Oh, no, nothing like that, thankfully. I mean... I've been maybe a little stressed, just from the things I mentioned, but definitely not depressed or hopeless. And I haven't been, like, overly energetic or skipping sleep either. 

I really try to keep a good, steady routine, you know? I still sleep my normal hours and everything. I hope that's okay to say—I just don't want you to think I'm, you know, falling apart or anything like that. I'm still doing really well at my job and keeping everything together. Does that answer your question alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Have you ever heard voices, sounds, or seen things that other people don't seem to notice or acknowledge?

Um, no, definitely not. I've never had anything like that happen. No voices or, you know, seeing things that aren't there. I know that's something people worry about, but I promise my mind is totally clear in that way. 

I mean, I'm just a regular guy who might be reading a little too much into some networking events, right? I'm definitely not... well, I'm not hearing things. I really hope that reassures you a bit? I just want to be absolutely sure you know I'm staying grounded. I'm answering these okay, aren't I?

Aside from these concerns about being watched, have you noticed any changes in how you think or express yourself—like trouble organizing your thoughts, speaking in a way others find hard to follow, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

Um... well... I wouldn't say my thoughts are disorganized or anything like that. I'm still communicating fine, I promise. But, um... I guess maybe I have been a little less... enthusiastic? Lately? 

I mean, I still get my work done, absolutely. Just... maybe in smaller pieces now. Sometimes I'll leave client follow-ups sitting a bit longer than I used to. And, um, I haven't really been going to my regular jazz nights or playing pickup basketball as much. It's not that I'm sad about missing them, it's just... I don't know, it just feels like a lot of effort right now. Even when my friends ask how I'm doing, I just kind of give them short answers. Talking just feels... heavier, I guess? 

But it's just a phase, right? I'm sure I'll bounce back soon. I'm not, like, completely withdrawing or anything. I just need a little time to recharge. Does that sound like a normal reaction to being stressed out? I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is.

Aside from feeling that people are tracking and signaling you at these events, have you had any other unusual beliefs—like thinking your thoughts are being read, controlled, or broadcast, or that you have special powers or a special mission?

Oh, gosh, no. No, definitely not. Um... I know my thoughts are entirely my own. Nobody is reading them or... or controlling them, and I certainly don't have any, like, special powers or a secret mission or anything like that. I'm just a regular guy, just a financial advisor trying to do a good job for his clients. 

I know me talking about the networking events might have sounded a little intense, but I promise I'm completely grounded otherwise. My mind is totally my own. I really hope that's a good sign? I just want to make sure you know I'm not losing my grip on reality or anything. Is that... is that the kind of answer you needed? I'm just trying to be as helpful and clear as I can.

You mentioned feeling less enthusiastic and pulling back from jazz nights and basketball—did that start around the same time as the tracking concerns two months ago, or did you notice that withdrawal beginning earlier?

Um... well... to be completely honest, it didn't start two months ago with the networking stuff. It's... it's been a bit longer than that. I hope it's okay that I didn't realize that right away. 

It's just been such a gradual thing, you know? Nothing drastic at all! Just sort of building up slowly. I guess... if I really sit down and think about it, these changes have been building since I got this recognition from an arts nonprofit I work with. That was, um, a little over two years ago now. 

I know two years sounds like a really long time to be in a bit of a slump, but I promise it hasn't been bad or anything. Just a slow shift where I've been a little less social and maybe a bit more tired. I'm still doing fine overall, really. Does that... does that timeline make sense to you? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of details here, I just want to make sure I'm answering everything properly.

Um... I'm so sorry, I don't think I quite caught what you just asked. Could you maybe repeat it for me? 

I haven't really noticed anything else unusual, if that's what you mean. I just want to make absolutely sure I'm giving you exactly the information you need. Is there something specific you want me to focus on? I promise I'm trying to be as helpful as I can, I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.

Over these past two years, has your day-to-day functioning changed in other ways—for example, has your work performance, ability to manage daily responsibilities, or self-care noticeably declined, or have you remained essentially as capable as before aside from feeling less social?

Oh, um... well, I'm definitely still working! I want to make sure you know that. My self-care and daily stuff at home are totally fine, I promise. 

As for work... well, I guess if I'm being completely honest, my practice has gotten a little bit smaller. But it's nothing terrible! It's just... I've missed a few follow-ups here and there, and I've been avoiding some of the public financial panels I used to speak on. It's just been a little harder lately to keep up the exact same level of client contact I used to manage before. 

But I'm still taking really good care of the clients I do have, I really am. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad advisor or like I'm failing at my job? I'm still very capable, just... maybe pacing myself a bit more and keeping a smaller roster right now. Is that... is that the kind of detail you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm being as open as you need me to be, and that I'm giving you the right picture.

Over these past two years, have you noticed that your range of emotional expression has become flatter or more muted—like friends commenting that you seem less expressive or that you show less emotion than you used to, even in situations unrelated to the tracking concerns?

Um... well... I wouldn't say "flatter," exactly. I hope I don't come across as, you know, completely emotionless or anything! I still feel things, I promise. 

It's just... maybe I don't have that same spark I used to? Like, I'll still get my work done, but just in pieces. And I'll leave some client follow-ups sitting for a bit, or I'll skip out on jazz nights or pickup basketball, and... I guess I just don't feel much about missing them. It's not that I'm depressed! Just... maybe a little less enthusiastic.

And, um, if friends ask what's going on, I might just give them really short answers. It's not because I don't care about them, I swear! It's just... lately, talking can feel like more effort than it really should. Does that make sense? I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad friend or anything. I'm still trying my best, I just... I hope I'm explaining this the right way for you?

When you think about how these people might be tracking or signaling you, does the explanation ever involve something that would be physically impossible—like hidden technology, mind-reading, or being monitored in ways beyond normal human means—or does it always feel like something that could plausibly happen in real life?

Oh, um... no, definitely not! I know how that sounds, and I promise it's nothing crazy like mind-reading or alien technology or anything like that. I'm a very logical person, you know? I deal with numbers and facts all day. 

It's just... it's all very normal stuff. Just people talking, maybe someone following me on the street, or leaving little signs. Things that could happen to anyone, really. I would never think anything impossible was happening. I know the difference between reality and, you know, movies. 

I hope that's the right answer? I just want you to know that I'm completely grounded in reality. I'm not... I'm not losing my mind or anything, I swear. Does that make sense? I'm trying really hard to be clear for you.
